title: Concurrent store opens fail with SQLITE_PROTOCOL after one retry in the next-ready race test
outcome: Concurrent store opens fail with SQLITE_PROTOCOL after one retry in the next-ready race test
acceptance: The cause of both caller threads in storage::work::execution::tests::next_ready::concurrent_callers_never_receive_the_same_child failing SqliteStore::open with FileLockingProtocolFailed (phase probe_snapshot, after one retry; src/storage/open_schema/protocol_retry.rs) is diagnosed with evidence (reproduction under the full lib suite's parallel load, SQLite WAL/shm behaviour on Windows, or a defect in the open path) and recorded.

The test passes reliably in full gates under the project's normal workload without loosening what it proves (two concurrent callers never receive the same child), or the defect it exposed is fixed; no retry-until-green and no skip.
disposal_reason: Per Greg #1592 (no small synthetic admission-attribution benchmarks; telemetry only when it informs a fix) and the holder's analysis (status 407d34d6): the existing harness drives SqliteStore open/next_ready, not control_status, so a loaded run would not change w-b64c's approved wrap-only status design. Archive retained. Residual production-phase telemetry after w-b64c lands would be separate work.
